solar_band.caveat: Bounds, not scenarios. Each level holds solar activity fixed at a percentile of the 1957-onward observed record for the whole run. No real 25-year period sits at one level -- the solar cycle is ~11 years, so a sustained solar maximum is physically impossible, not merely unlikely. Read low/high as bounds the true answer lies between, and never as best-case and worst-case futures.

designs.label: no-chassis-stated
designs.prose: A radar earth observation platform at 693 km, 65 degrees, 4.8 kW, seven year mission.

mission_duration_years.detail: disposal clock starts at end of mission (47 CFR 25.283(e))

cd.detail: Free-molecular convention from data/satellite_specs.json (swept 2.0-2.4 elsewhere). Not a spec input.

dry_mass_kg.detail: 4800 W lies outside the reference range for this class. comparable spacecraft vary by 3.6x in kg/W (class basis, n=6), above the 2.0x limit. At this spread power does not determine mass, so no interpolation on power can resolve it.

sources.name: Himawari-8
sources.source: eoPortal, Himawari-8 and 9; Gunter's Space Page

ram_area_knife_edge_m2.detail: No chassis dimensions were stated, so sim/geometry.py has nothing to solve. Ram area is not assumed from a typical bus: that would put a fabricated number into the drag term.

ram_area_broadside_m2.detail: No chassis dimensions were stated, so sim/geometry.py has nothing to solve. Ram area is not assumed from a typical bus: that would put a fabricated number into the drag term.

ballistic_coefficient_kg_m2.detail: needs a ram area, which needs a stated chassis.

orbit.note: Ground track is illustrative display geometry. Inclination and altitude are the spec's and the period is computed from them, but lat/lon modelling is outside the validated physics (PHYSICS.md §1).

designs.label: underspecified
designs.prose: Something like a Starlink but a bit bigger.

questions.question: What circular altitude should the satellite operate at, in km?
questions.why: Altitude drives atmospheric density over about four orders of magnitude across LEO; nothing downstream is meaningful without it.

questions.question: What orbital inclination, in degrees?
questions.why: Inclination sets the latitude at which density is sampled (PHYSICS.md §10.2). Sun-synchronous is not enough on its own: its inclination depends on altitude through J2, which this engine does not model (PHYSICS.md §1).

questions.question: What is the payload -- earth observation, communications, navigation, or a technology demonstration?
questions.why: Communications satellites are roughly 3x lighter per watt than instrument-carrying ones, so the class picks which reference spacecraft the mass is interpolated between.

questions.question: What is the spacecraft's electrical power, in watts?
questions.why: Power is the predictor the mass model interpolates on (sim/mass_model.py). Without it there is no mass, and without a mass there is no ballistic coefficient and no verdict.

questions.question: How long is the operational mission, in years?
questions.why: The disposal clock starts at end of mission (47 CFR 25.283(e)), so the duration sets when the compliance window opens.

designs.blocked: The description does not determine a spec. The engine was not run; these are the questions that stand between the prose and a design.
